confirmed.title: Tabs stay fully visible during sheet moves on deep-link and reduced-motion loads: the pre-hydration rule `.js-tabs{opacity:1 !important}` overrides the fade
confirmed.expected: While a sheet is moving, the tab layer has opacity 0 and pointer-events none (transition opacity .2s), so the tabs never paint over the sheet sliding out.
confirmed.actual: On any load with data-intro='skip' (a deep link such as /#crumbify, /#cv, or a prefers-reduced-motion load), `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs { opacity: 1 !important; }` stays in force for the whole session. During every bring(), the inline opacity is '0' but the computed opacity is '1'. The tabs (z 9) come after the moving-out sheet (also z 9) in the DOM, so they paint on top of it.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright on /#crumbify, click the 'about' tab, then read after 250ms: nav.style.opacity='0', getComputedStyle(nav).opacity='1', pointerEvents='none'. The same check on a fresh '/' load after the intro gives computed opacity '0'. Reduced-motion load on '/': computed opacity '1' during the move. Screenshot deeplink-move.png shows the tab strip drawn over the About sheet as it slides out. The rule has no purpose here because the tabs are never in the static HTML: they only render when phase==='done'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Delete the `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs` rule in src/app/globals.css:62-64. Add an e2e assertion that the tab layer's computed opacity is 0 mid-move on a /#crumbify load.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: globals.css:62-64 `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs{opacity:1 !important}` beats the inline style from Tabs.tsx:41. Measured live on /#crumbify (1280x900): clicked the desktop 'about' tab and read the nav after 250ms. Inline opacity was '0', computed opacity '1', pointer-events 'none'. On a fresh '/' load after the intro, the same check gives computed '0'. The rule is dead weight: Pile.tsx:57/77 only renders Tabs when phase==='done', so no tab exists in the static HTML for it to guard. atn-17 fails on every deep-link or reduced-motion session.
confirmed.fix: Delete the `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs { opacity: 1 !important; }` block at src/app/globals.css:62-64, and drop the reference to it in the Tabs.tsx:21-22 doc comment. Add an e2e test: load /#crumbify, click a tab, and at about 200ms assert getComputedStyle(nav[data-variant=desktop]).opacity === '0'.

confirmed.title: Deep links keep document.title 'Ali Bars': Next's metadata resets it about 40ms after Pile sets the sheet title
confirmed.expected: Loading /#racing gives the title 'City Racing · Ali Bars', /#about gives 'About · Ali Bars', and so on.
confirmed.actual: On a deep-link load, the title is 'Ali Bars' from then on. Pile's effect sets it correctly, then the <title> node is rewritten back to the static metadata title (layout.tsx:28). It only corrects itself after a later bring().
confirmed.evidence: Traced document.title writes with a setter hook plus a MutationObserver. On /#racing: set 'City Racing · Ali Bars' at 360ms (page chunk), then a mutation back to 'Ali Bars' at 403ms. /#about: set at 445ms, reset at 483ms. /#video: set at 379ms, reset at 452ms. page.title() is still 'Ali Bars' at 2s. After clicking the 'about' tab, the title correctly becomes 'About · Ali Bars'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Let React own the title: render `{phase === 'done' ? <title>{sheetTitles[top]}</title> : null}` inside Pile (React 19 hoists it), or re-apply document.title after hydration settles, e.g. in a requestAnimationFrame. Add an e2e check of the title on a /#racing load.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Measured live: /#racing, /#about and /#video each give page.title()==='Ali Bars' 4s after load, not 'City Racing · Ali Bars' etc. (content.ts:280-286). After clicking the 'about' tab the title correctly becomes 'About · Ali Bars', so the effect at Pile.tsx:32-34 works, but on the initial deep-link load it is overwritten by the static metadata title from layout.tsx:28. bh-16 fails for deep links.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Pile.tsx, stop the imperative write from being clobbered. Either render `{phase === 'done' ? <title>{sheetTitles[top]}</title> : null}` inside Pile's JSX (React 19 hoists it and owns it), or re-apply the title after hydration, e.g. `requestAnimationFrame(() => { document.title = sheetTitles[top]; })` inside the existing effect. Add an e2e test: goto /#racing, wait, expect(page).toHaveTitle('City Racing · Ali Bars').

confirmed.title: A deep link paints the CV sheet first, then swaps to the requested sheet at hydration
confirmed.expected: A deep link such as /#about opens that sheet directly, with no frame of a different sheet before it (same spirit as the no-title-flash guard).
confirmed.actual: The static HTML always renders top='cv'. The pre-hydration script hides only the title page and un-offsets the stage, so until the JS chunks load and the layout effect runs, the first paint shows the CV on top. The About sheet then replaces it.
confirmed.evidence: /#about with /_next/static/chunks/** blocked (the pre-hydration state): data-intro='skip', the title page has display:none, and the only visible article is 'sheet-cv' (about-nojs.png).
confirmed.suggestedFix: In the pre-hydration script, also set data-top=<hash sheet>. Add CSS such as `:root[data-top]:not([data-top='cv']) #sheet-cv { visibility:hidden }`, so the pre-hydration frame shows the bare pile rather than the wrong sheet. Or accept this and log it in implementation-notes.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Loaded /#about live with /_next/static/chunks/** aborted, to freeze the pre-hydration frame. data-intro='skip', and the only visible article is sheet-cv (z 10). The static HTML always renders top='cv' (usePile.ts:42 SSR_STATE), and layout.tsx:44-53 only sets data-intro and data-desk, so the first paint of any non-CV deep link shows the CV, which is then swapped at the layout effect. extra-intro-19 only covers the title-page flash, so this is a minor sibling flash: real, but low.
confirmed.fix: In the src/app/layout.tsx pre-hydration script, also call d.setAttribute('data-top', hash) when the hash is a sheet id. In globals.css add `:root[data-intro='skip'][data-top]:not([data-top='cv']) #sheet-cv { visibility: hidden; }`, and remove data-top (or make the rule moot) once React has hydrated, e.g. removeAttribute in usePile's mount layout effect. Alternatively, log it as an accepted limitation in docs/implementation-notes.md.

confirmed.title: On a dark first paint the toggle reads 'Lights off' on the dark desk until hydration
confirmed.expected: The first painted frame with a stored or OS dark preference shows the dark desk and the label 'Lights on'.
confirmed.actual: The static HTML always contains 'Lights off' (useTheme initialises to false). The desk is dark from first paint, but the label is wrong until the JS loads and the layout effect runs.
confirmed.evidence: Load with localStorage alibars-desk='dark' and the JS chunks blocked: data-desk='dark', a gradient desk, header button textContent 'Lights off' (dark-stored-nojs.png). The same happens for an OS-dark load: data-desk='dark', label 'Lights off'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Render both labels in spans and show one with CSS keyed on :root[data-desk] (e.g. `[data-desk='dark'] .labelLight{display:none}`), or render the label client-only.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Loaded live with JS chunks blocked, first with localStorage alibars-desk='dark' and then with colorScheme 'dark'. Both gave data-desk='dark' but a header button label of 'Lights off'. useTheme.ts:23 initialises dark=false and Desk.tsx:16 renders that label into the static HTML. The label is only corrected by the layout effect after hydration, so the first paint breaks gl-10 on the dark desk (extra-gl-32 expects the first frame to be correct).
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Desk.tsx, render both labels, e.g. `Lights offLights on`. In Desk.module.css (or globals.css) add `:root[data-desk='dark'] .labelLight{display:none}` and `:root:not([data-desk='dark']) .labelDark{display:none}`. Keep the accessible name correct: the hidden span is display:none, so it is excluded.

confirmed.title: When localStorage access throws, the whole pre-hydration script aborts: the OS dark preference is ignored and deep links flash the title page
confirmed.expected: With storage blocked, there is no stored value, so the desk follows prefers-color-scheme: dark, and a deep link still skips the title page from the first paint.
confirmed.actual: `localStorage.getItem` throws a SecurityError when site data is blocked. It sits inside the single try block, so neither data-desk nor data-intro is set. useTheme only reads data-desk, so an OS-dark user gets the light desk for the whole session. Before hydration, /#about paints the title page and the pile at translateX(-130vw).
confirmed.evidence: Blocked storage (window.localStorage getter throws) with colorScheme 'dark', on /#about with JS blocked: data-desk undefined, data-intro undefined, title page display 'flex', stage transform 'translateX(-130vw)'. After hydration: data-desk undefined, label 'Lights off', body background-image 'none' (light desk), even though the OS prefers dark.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Put the storage read in its own try/catch (`var stored=null; try{stored=localStorage.getItem(...)}catch(e){}`), then run the matchMedia and data-intro logic unconditionally. In useTheme's layout effect, fall back to matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') when data-desk is missing.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Measured live with an init script that makes the window.localStorage getter throw a SecurityError, plus colorScheme 'dark', on /#about. After hydration: data-desk undefined, data-intro undefined, label 'Lights off'. The light desk is shown even though the OS prefers dark, which breaks gl-28. The cause is that layout.tsx:44-53 wraps everything in one try block, and the getItem on line 46 throws first. useTheme.ts:32 only reads data-desk, with no matchMedia fallback. The title page did end up absent after hydration, because usePile resolves the skip itself, but the pre-hydration guard for extra-intro-19 is also lost.
confirmed.fix: In the src/app/layout.tsx preHydrationScript, change it to `var stored=null; try{stored=localStorage.getItem('alibars-desk');}catch(e){}`, then run the matchMedia dark and data-intro logic outside that inner try, keeping the outer try only as a final guard. Optionally, in useTheme.ts:31-35, fall back to window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches when data-desk is absent, and set the attribute.

confirmed.title: Dismissing the title page with the keyboard drops focus to <body>, and the next Tab skips the whole CV
confirmed.expected: After Enter or Space on the focused title page, focus lands somewhere sensible on the CV (e.g. the CV sheet container, as Pile.tsx:41-47 already does after bring()), so keyboard users continue from the revealed page.
confirmed.actual: The title page unmounts at phase 'done' while focused. activeElement becomes BODY, and Chrome's focus starting point moves past the CV sheet, so the next Tab lands on the 'cv' divider tab and every CV control is skipped.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright: three Tabs put focus on 'TitlePage_titlePage js-title-page', Enter, wait 1300ms, then activeElement is 'BODY'. The next Tab focuses 'BUTTON cv' (the desktop tab), not the CV's first link.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In Pile.tsx, when phase moves from 'pull' to 'done' and document.activeElement is body (or the title was focused), call document.getElementById(`sheet-${top}`)?.focus({preventScroll:true}). Or extend the existing focus effect so it also fires on the intro-to-done transition, not only after touched.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Measured live on '/': focused .js-title-page, pressed Enter, waited 1400ms. document.activeElement was BODY and the next Tab focused 'BUTTON cv' (the desktop tab), skipping every CV control. Pile.tsx:41-47 only moves focus when `top` changes and `touched` is set, and neither holds on the intro-to-done transition, while the title page unmounts at Pile.tsx:78-80.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Pile.tsx, add an effect keyed on phase. Track the previous phase in a ref, and when it goes from 'pull' to 'done' and document.activeElement === document.body, call document.getElementById(`sheet-${top}`)?.focus({ preventScroll: true }). The sheet article already has tabIndex=-1 from the behaviour-08 fix. Add an e2e test: Tab to the title page, press Enter, wait 1.3s, press Tab, and expect focus inside #sheet-cv.

confirmed.title: REGRESSION: in dark mode, CV contact links get a near-white focus outline (#e8e4dc) on #fbfaf6 paper, because CvHeader is a <header>
confirmed.expected: Controls on paper sheets keep the dark 2px #1c1b19 focus outline in dark mode. That is the whole point of the slice-04 fix and the comment at globals.css:112-115.
confirmed.actual: The slice-04 fix scoped the light outline with `[data-desk='dark'] header :focus-visible`. The CV sheet's header block is also a `<header>` (src/components/sheets/CvHeader.tsx:6), so it matches too. In dark mode the email, LinkedIn and GitHub contact links get outline-color rgb(232,228,220) on the rgb(251,250,246) paper, which makes the focus ring close to invisible.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright on out/ at 1280px, /#cv, with data-desk='dark' and keyboard focus on 'alibars999@gmail.com': getComputedStyle(activeElement).outlineColor = 'rgb(232, 228, 220)', outlineStyle 'solid'. `grep '<header' src` finds both Desk.tsx:10 (the desk header, the intended target) and CvHeader.tsx:6.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Scope the selector to the desk header only. For example, use `[data-desk='dark'] .<Desk header class> :focus-visible` inside Desk.module.css (`:global([data-desk='dark']) .header :focus-visible`), or change CvHeader's root element from <header> to <div>. Add an e2e assertion that the focus outline on a CV contact link in dark mode is rgb(28,27,25).
confirmed.verifyReasoning: globals.css:116 selector `[data-desk='dark'] header :focus-visible` also matches the CV sheet's own <header> (src/components/sheets/CvHeader.tsx:6); grep finds both Desk.tsx:10 and CvHeader.tsx:6. Reproduced live on out/ (port 5202) at 1280 and 320px: with data-desk='dark' on <html> and keyboard focus on the 'alibars999@gmail.com' link, the computed outlineColor is rgb(232, 228, 220) (= --desk-ink-dark #e8e4dc), not #1c1b19, on light paper. The screenshot shows the ring is barely visible. This breaks gl-24 and the stated intent of the comment at globals.css:112-115.
confirmed.fix: In src/app/globals.css:116, scope the rule to the desk header only. Either change the CV header root in src/components/sheets/CvHeader.tsx:6 from <header> to <div> (keep className and adjust the closing tag), or replace the global rule with `:global([data-desk='dark']) .header :focus-visible { outline-color: var(--desk-ink-dark); }` in the Desk header's CSS module and delete globals.css:116-118. Add an e2e assertion that the focus outline on a CV contact link is rgb(28, 27, 25) in dark mode.

confirmed.title: Internal CV highlights are atomic inline-block <button>s: they wrap as a centred block and add 2px to each highlight row
confirmed.expected: Prototype: the highlight is an inline <span> with padding 1px 5px. The padding does not grow the line box, the text wraps inline and stays left-aligned, and the gradient breaks across lines. cv-26 allows a <button> only if it keeps 'the highlight look inline'.
confirmed.actual: `.highlight{display:inline}` has no effect on a <button>, which computes to display:inline-block with the UA default text-align:center. (1) At 320px, 'Data Acquisition & Firmware Engineer →' becomes a 2-line, 238px-wide yellow block with the second line 'Engineer →' centred. The footer 'motorsport / F1, music, esports →' drops to its own line as a single unit instead of wrapping after 'Off the page:'. (2) At every width, each highlight's entry row is 2px taller than with the prototype's inline span (for example 26.20px vs 24.20px at 1280, and 23.67px vs 21.67px at 390).
confirmed.evidence: Playwright on out/ at 1280, 390 and 320px. Button computed display 'inline-block', text-align 'center'. At 320px the Racing highlight button is 42.79px tall × 238px wide. Replacing each button with an inline span of the same class (prototype markup) measures the entry row at 2px shorter at every width, and gives getClientRects().length=2 (inline wrap) for the Racing and footer highlights. Screenshots: scratchpad/review-r2/slice-cv-crumbify/racing-hl-320.png (centred two-line block) and footer-320.png.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Render internal highlights as `<a href="#<id>">` with an onClick that calls preventDefault() and then onOpen(). cv-26 explicitly allows this, and an <a> stays a true inline box. Add `box-decoration-break: clone` if needed. At minimum, add `text-align: inherit` to `.highlight` so wrapped text is not centred.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Highlight.tsx renders internal highlights as <button>. `.highlight{display:inline}` (Highlight.module.css:11) does not make a button a true inline box: measured live, the computed display is 'inline-block' and text-align is 'center'. At 320px the 'Data Acquisition & Firmware Engineer →' button is a 238x43px two-line block. Buttons are 23px tall, while the prototype's inline span with 1px padding would not grow the line box. The spec (README:91 'Highlight span base', README:238 'real <button>s (or <a href="#crumbify">) styled inline') and cv-26 ('keeping the highlight look inline') require inline behaviour, so centred block wrapping is a concrete mismatch. It only shows visually at narrow widths, so severity stays low.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/Highlight.tsx, render internal highlights as `<a href={`#${id}`} onClick={e => { e.preventDefault(); props.onOpen(); }} className=...>` (this needs a target id passed in, or keep onOpen and use href='#'+sheet id). An <a> keeps display:inline so it wraps inline and the gradient breaks per line. Add `box-decoration-break: clone; -webkit-box-decoration-break: clone;` to .highlight in Highlight.module.css if per-line padding is wanted. At minimum, if a <button> is kept, add `text-align: inherit;` to .highlight in Highlight.module.css so wrapped text is not centred.

confirmed.title: On deep-link and reduced-motion loads the divider tabs never fade out during a sheet move (the data-intro='skip' rule forces opacity:1)
confirmed.expected: While moving is non-null the tab layer is opacity:0 with pointer-events:none, and it fades back in after 960ms (README 'Divider tabs': the whole tab layer is opacity:0 while a sheet is moving; transition opacity .2s).
confirmed.actual: The pre-hydration script (src/app/layout.tsx:52) sets data-intro='skip' on <html> for any deep link (/#racing, /#about, /#cv...) or reduced-motion load, and nothing ever removes it. The rule ':root[data-intro="skip"] .js-tabs { opacity: 1 !important; }' then beats the inline opacity:0 from Tabs.tsx:41 for the whole session. The tabs stay fully visible (but can't be clicked, because pointer-events:none still applies) over the pile while the new sheet slides out and back in. On a fresh '/' load (data-intro='play') the same move fades correctly. This rule came in with the round-1 hydration fixes.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright against out/ on port 5103, 1280x1000. Loaded /#racing, clicked the 'about' tab, and sampled the desktop nav every 120ms: inline style.opacity='0' but getComputedStyle opacity='1' in all 6 samples, pointer-events 'none'. The same check on a fresh '/' load after dismissing the title page gave computed opacity 1, 0.126, 0, 0, 0, 0. Loading /#about and clicking 'racing': data-intro='skip', inline '0', computed '1'. A reduced-motion '/' load gave the same result. The mid-move screenshot mid-deep.png shows all 5 tabs painted while the Racing sheet is off to the right. The built CSS contains '.js-tabs{opacity:1!important}'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Delete the ':root[data-intro="skip"] .js-tabs' rule in src/app/globals.css:62-64. The tabs are not in the static HTML (they only render at phase 'done'), so the rule has no pre-hydration job. Alternatively, remove the data-intro attribute in usePile's mount layout effect once phase is resolved. Add an e2e test: load /#racing, click a tab, and assert that the nav's computed opacity reaches 0 mid-move.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: src/app/globals.css:62-64 declares `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs { opacity: 1 !important; }`. layout.tsx:52 sets data-intro='skip' for any deep-link hash or reduced motion, and nothing in src removes it (grep: the only data-intro references are globals.css:56/59/62, layout.tsx:52 and comments). Tabs.tsx:41 hides the tabs during a move with an inline, non-important `opacity: 0`. An author `!important` declaration beats an inline normal declaration in the cascade, so on skip loads the tab layer stays at opacity 1 for the whole session while a sheet moves. That contradicts README:193 ('While a sheet is moving: the whole tab layer is opacity:0; pointer-events:none'). pointer-events has no !important rule, so it still switches to none, which matches the reviewer's evidence. The tabs only mount after hydration, so the rule has no pre-hydration job to do.
confirmed.fix: Delete the `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs { opacity: 1 !important; }` block at src/app/globals.css:62-64, and remove the reference to it in the comment at src/components/Tabs.tsx:22. Add an e2e test: load /#racing, click the 'about' tab, and assert that the computed opacity of nav[data-variant=desktop] reaches 0 during the move.

confirmed.title: Racing 'Live telemetry.' and 'GPS lap tool (C++).' leads use <strong> (computed weight 700) instead of 600
confirmed.expected: The bold leads are <span style="font-weight:600"> in the prototype (Interactive CV v3.dc.html, racing section), so the computed font-weight is 600. Round 1 fixed the same issue on the CV (slice-cv-06, now 600-weight spans).
confirmed.actual: RacingSheet.tsx:22 and :27 render <strong>, and no CSS rule sets its weight (RacingSheet.module.css has no strong/lead rule), so the UA default font-weight:bold (700) applies. IBM Plex Sans is only loaded at 400/500/600 (layout.tsx:7), so the browser falls back to the 600 face or synthesises bold instead of honouring the spec value.
confirmed.evidence: getComputedStyle on #sheet-racing strong, for both elements: font-weight '700'. Source: '{racing.telemetry.lead}' at line 22 and '{racing.gps.lead}' at line 27.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Replace <strong> with <span className={styles.lead}> and add .lead { font-weight: 600; } to RacingSheet.module.css, as CvSheet did for slice-cv-06, or add '.paragraph strong { font-weight: 600; }'.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: RacingSheet.tsx:22 and :27 render `{...lead}`. No CSS in src sets a weight on strong (grep finds no strong or bold rule in any .css file), so the UA's `bolder` value applies and resolves to 700 on a 400 base. The prototype (Interactive CV v3.dc.html:85 and :87) uses `Live telemetry.` and `GPS lap tool (C++).`, so the spec weight is 600.
confirmed.fix: In src/components/sheets/RacingSheet.module.css add `.paragraph strong { font-weight: 600; }`, or replace both <strong> elements (RacingSheet.tsx:22, :27) with `<span className={styles.lead}>` and add `.lead { font-weight: 600; }`.

confirmed.title: The mobile (<600px) tab row has no opacity transition, so it blinks off and on instantly during every move
confirmed.expected: The tab layer fades with transition:opacity .2s when a move starts and ends (README 'Divider tabs'), and that applies to whichever tab layer is visible, including the recommended horizontal row below 600px.
confirmed.actual: 'transition: opacity 0.2s' is only declared on .tabsDesktop (Tabs.module.css:6). .tabsMobile (lines 47-54) has none, so the mobile nav's inline opacity toggles 1 to 0 to 1 with no fade.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright at 390x800 on /#cv: getComputedStyle(nav[data-variant=mobile]).transition = 'all' (the initial value, 0s duration). At 1280 wide, the desktop nav reports 'opacity 0.2s'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Move 'transition: opacity 0.2s' into a rule shared by both variants (e.g. add it to .tabsMobile inside the media query, or to a common nav class).
confirmed.verifyReasoning: In src/components/Tabs.module.css, `transition: opacity 0.2s` appears only on .tabsDesktop (line 6). .tabsMobile (lines 38-54, including the <600px media block) declares no transition. The shared inline opacity toggle in Tabs.tsx:41 therefore switches the mobile row from 1 to 0 and back instantly. README:193 specifies `transition:opacity .2s` for the tab layer, and implementation-notes does not exempt the mobile row.
confirmed.fix: Add `transition: opacity 0.2s;` to the .tabsMobile rule inside `@media (max-width: 599px)` in src/components/Tabs.module.css (around line 47), or move it to a rule shared by both nav variants.

confirmed.title: On deep-link and reduced-motion loads the tabs never fade out during a move ([data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs opacity:1 !important stays forever)

confirmed.actual: data-intro='skip' is never removed from <html>. The pre-hydration override `opacity: 1 !important` therefore beats the inline opacity:0 for the whole session, and the tabs stay fully visible during every move on any deep-link or reduced-motion load. confirmed.verifyReasoning: globals.css:62-64 `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs { opacity: 1 !important }` and nothing ever removes data-intro. This violates the README's rule that the tab layer is at opacity 0 while a sheet moves (bh-03 area).
confirmed.fix: Delete the `:root[data-intro='skip'] .js-tabs { opacity: 1 !important; }` rule from src/app/globals.css:62-64. Tabs only render when phase==='done', so there is nothing to protect before hydration. Or, alternatively, call document.documentElement.removeAttribute('data-intro') at the end of the mount useLayoutEffect in src/lib/usePile.ts.

confirmed.title: Reduced motion: the 'instant' cross-fade only starts 440ms after the click (the incoming sheet is invisible for the whole out stage)
confirmed.expected: With prefers-reduced-motion, a sheet swap is an instant cross-fade: the new sheet starts fading in right away.
confirmed.actual: The 440/960ms timers still run unchanged. In 'out' the incoming sheet is opacity 0 under the current top (z m+1), so nothing visible happens for 440ms. It then fades in 0 -> 1 over 200ms at z m+3, and the swap settles at 960ms. The user sees a ~0.45s dead delay after each click.
confirmed.evidence: RM trace for a CV -> About swap (25ms samples): 0-251ms about z9 opacity 1 -> 0 (hidden under the CV at z10); 477ms about z11 opacity 0.07; 676ms opacity 1; 1002ms CV hidden, about z10. The transform is identity throughout (no slide, correct).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Under reducedMotion, have bring() go straight to stage 'in' (skipping 'out'), or shorten the timers (e.g. in at 0ms, settle at 200ms), so the fade begins right away.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Live, reduced motion, CV to About via tab: the about sheet goes to opacity 0 at z 9 from 0 to 430ms (hidden under the CV), then fades in at z 11 from about 434 to 625ms, and settles at z 10 at around 1039ms. So the cross-fade only starts about 440ms after the click. pile.ts:88-90 plus the unchanged 440/960 timers in usePile.ts bring(). The README says to make sheet swaps an 'instant cross-fade', and a 0.44s dead delay does not meet that.
confirmed.fix: In src/lib/usePile.ts bring(): when reducedMotion is true, set moving stage 'in' immediately (skip 'out') and settle at 200ms (matching the 0.2s opacity transition in Sheet.module.css:26), i.e. `at(reduced ? 0 : 440, ...)` and `at(reduced ? 200 : 960, ...)`. Or use the 'in' stage directly in the initial setState when reduced.

confirmed.title: Browser Back pressed during an in-flight move is dropped, then a pushState restores the old hash and wipes forward history
confirmed.expected: Back pressed while a sheet is moving still takes effect (queued, or applied after the move settles), and the URL and pile stay in sync.
confirmed.actual: onHashChange calls bring(), and canBring rejects it while moving !== null. When the move settles, useHashSync sees top changed and the URL hash differs, so it pushState()s the moving sheet's hash back. Back appears to do nothing, forward history is truncated, and a double Back lands on the wrong sheet.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright on out/: from /#racing click the 'about' tab, then 200ms later page.goBack(): after 1.5s the URL is '#about' and the title is 'About · Ali Bars' (expected racing). In another run: racing, then video, then Back twice within 100ms: the page ends on '#racing' with history.length back to 3, so the /#video entry is destroyed and the CV is never reached.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In usePileKeys' onHashChange, when canBring would reject because a move is in flight, store the requested sheet in a ref and bring() it when the move settles (in the 960ms callback or an effect on moving===null). Or make useHashSync skip pushing when the hash changed externally during the move. Add a unit test: bring('crumbify'), dispatch hashchange to '' at 200ms, advance timers, and expect top 'cv'.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: usePile.ts:89-91 onHashChange calls bring(), which canBring rejects while moving is not null. When the move settles, useHashSync (usePile.ts:77-79) sees top != hash and pushState()s it back. Reproduced live: /#cv, click racing, settle (#racing, history.length 3), click about, then goBack() 200ms later. After 1.5s the URL is /#about, the title is 'About · Ali Bars', aria-current is 'about' and history.length is 3, so the forward entry was overwritten and Back was lost.
confirmed.fix: src/lib/usePile.ts: add a pendingRef. In onHashChange, if stateRef.current.moving !== null, store sheetFromHash(location.hash) ?? 'cv' in pendingRef instead of calling bring. In the 960ms settle callback, or in a useEffect on state.moving === null, if pendingRef is set and differs from top, clear it and call bring(pending). useHashSync must not push while a pending external hash exists. Add a unit test: bring('crumbify'), set the hash to '' and dispatch hashchange at 200ms, run all timers, and expect top 'cv' with the URL left without a hash.

confirmed.title: useTimers never prunes fired timer ids, and its comment wrongly calls it 'Debounced'
confirmed.expected: Timer ids are removed once they fire (or the array is reset per move), and the doc comment matches the behaviour.
confirmed.actual: at() pushes every id into timers.current, which only shrinks on pull() or unmount. Every bring() adds 2 stale ids for the life of the page. Nothing debounces anything, despite the 'Debounced setTimeout scheduling' comment.
confirmed.evidence: src/lib/usePile.ts:45-60: `timers.current.push(setTimeout(fn, ms))`, cleared only in clearTimers (called from pull and the unmount effect).
confirmed.suggestedFix: In at(), wrap fn so it removes its own id from timers.current when it fires (return a new filtered array), and reword the comment to 'setTimeout scheduling that clears pending timers on unmount'.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: usePile.ts:48-50 pushes every timeout id into timers.current, which is only reset in clearTimers (pull or unmount). Every bring() adds 2 ids that are never removed. The growth is negligible, but real. The line-44 comment 'Debounced setTimeout scheduling' is wrong: nothing debounces. This is code quality only, with no user-visible effect.
confirmed.fix: src/lib/usePile.ts:48-50: `const id = setTimeout(() => { timers.current = timers.current.filter(t => t !== id); fn(); }, ms); timers.current = [...timers.current, id];`. Change the line-44 comment to 'setTimeout scheduling whose pending timers are cleared on pull() and on unmount.'
